name: Cairo by Night: Factions and Mysteries

text.content:
The Ashirra — Islamic Kindred bound by a shared faith rather than sect or clan — form the largest single vampiric grouping in Cairo, claiming between 80 and 100 members at any time in a city whose mortal and vampire population is overwhelmingly Muslim. Unlike other sects, the Ashirra’s charter is purely religious: members hold to Islam and its Five Pillars of Faith (the Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm, and Hajj) as best they can manage as the Damned, with most treating outright observance of the fast and the pilgrimage to Mecca as either impossible or suicidal given the risks True Faith poses to vampires. The Ashirra is led in Cairo by Ibn Ja’far the Golden, a Nosferatu who has guided the city’s Muslim Kindred for nearly eight centuries and remains one of Cairo’s most influential and respected figures despite a private crisis of faith few know about.

The Hajj is the Ashirra’s most devout inner circle — specifically the Muslim Nosferatu of Cairo, who consider themselves the “first circle” of Islam among the Damned. Founded by Ibn Ja’far following Salah al-Din’s death in 1193, the Hajj alone still observes all five daily prayers and, controversially, still undertakes the pilgrimage to Mecca (a practice virtually every other Ashirra considers suicidal), visiting the sect’s founder Tarique to learn directly from him. This orthodoxy has widened the gulf between the Hajj and their more pragmatic Muslim brethren. The Hajj also serve as the city’s guides to its many zones of Ambient Faith, a duty they inherited from a Setite merchant named Bilaal and now perform with genuine pride, charging no fee but gathering considerable intelligence on visiting Kindred in the process.

pages.name: The Osirian League and the Rite of the Sun King

text.content:
The Osirian League was an ancient order of vampires (and, some say, other beings) sworn to oppose the Followers of Set’s millennia-old bid to dominate Egypt through corruption of its rulers. Its founder, a Gangrel calling himself Anpu, blamed himself for a lapse that let the Cult of Isis’s Spell of Life fall into Set’s hands, birthing the seven Bane Mummies, and he dedicated his unlife to atonement and revenge. Anpu’s masterwork was the Rite of the Sun King: a rite that permanently barred Setite corruption, magic (including Thaumaturgical Akhu and Serpentis itself), and even the physical presence of Set’s childer from a vast zone covering all of Lower Egypt.

The rite required a perpetual anchor: a mortal or vampire of extraordinary character who would maintain it from beyond death. Anpu chose Queen Hatshepsut, subjecting her to both the Cult of Isis’s Spell of Life and the Rite of the Sun King upon her death, then having her secretly interred at Deir al-Bahari (her mortuary temple near Luxor) under guard of Anpu’s own bloodline, the Disciples of Anubis. For millennia the rite held, crippling the Followers of Set’s influence over Lower Egypt’s rulers and keeping the clan’s Egyptian courts largely marginalized and resentful.

The rite’s protections shattered in 1999, coinciding with the destruction of the House of Peace (the Children of Osiris’ stronghold) and opening the door for the Followers of Set’s Court of Dust and Bone at Wadi Natrun to attempt to seize control of the Dream Court’s sleeping Methuselah while it lies vulnerable — a plot still unfolding as the Final Nights approach.

pages.name: The Dream Court and the Sleeping Lord

text.content:
Beneath Cairo’s sewers, medieval aqueducts, and byways lies the Dream Court: the second-largest Temple of Set in the world, a vast, dreamlike labyrinth ruled by the Sleeping Lord, also called the Maiden of Plagues. This entity is a childe of the Scorpion King, a Setite lord annihilated ages ago by the goddess Sakhmet, whose blood curse struck down or maddened every one of the Scorpion King’s own childer in retribution — the Maiden of Plagues alone survived, cursed to a slow, dissolving decay and unable to Embrace viable childer of her own ever since. At over 5,000 years old, she is believed by her attendants to maintain a unique dreaming contact with the sleeping Set himself.

Since the Assamite elder Antara sealed her maddening presence within the tunnels roughly 150 years ago, the Dream Court’s Setites have brought the city to her instead, through a rite called the Reverie: drugged, hypnotized mortals are led into the depths to bask in her presence and carry her influence back to the surface, with some repeatedly harvested until they become mindless agents called thralls. The court’s outer perimeter is guarded by twisted, biting creatures that the Setite elder Kahina learned to attune to recognize those who belong.

The Sleeping Lord’s one hope of escaping Sakhmet’s curse rests on a prophesied Caitiff woman known as the Herald, said to be the One With Child — the Dream Court has made her acquisition its top priority, unaware that the Herald and her fate may be entwined with the imprisoned entity sealed within the artifact called Lot 14.

When the Tremere of Cairo’s Egyptian Museum chantry uncovered a previously uncharted temple in the Western Desert near Wadi Natrun (the “Shenouda Cache”), one crated relic — a sealed white-stone canopic jar labeled Lot 14 and covered in untranslated hieroglyphs — fell into the hands of the chantry’s curatrix, Hyapatia. After months of obsessive study she broke the seal, releasing what she believes to be a djinn from the Realm of Smokeless Fire, eager to reward her for its freedom.

In truth, Lot 14 imprisons the entombed essence of the Lord of the Dream Court itself, sealed away by the sorcerers of the fallen Setite temple that once stood in the Western Desert. The entity has spent every night since manipulating the smitten Hyapatia, fostering her romantic delusions and steering her toward a Tremere power grab, all while it schemes for its own release. Hyapatia’s chantry sire, Kasper von Aupfholme, vanished investigating the same temple and has not been heard from since — a disappearance the Followers of Set’s agent Kahina has quietly confirmed to Sylvia Kilver, the chantry’s ambitious acting regent, who is maneuvering to claim the regency once Hyapatia’s folly with Lot 14 becomes public.

pages.name: The House of Peace and the Children of Osiris

text.content:
For over a century, the Dar es Salaam (“House of Peace”) stood on Sharia Mohammed Farid as the global headquarters of the Children of Osiris, a bloodline devoted to preserving ma’at (cosmic and personal balance) against the Beast within, and a key pillar of the Osirian League’s ancient war against the Followers of Set. The four-story manor sheltered more than 30 Children of every prior clan and background under a strict policy of never turning away one of their own in need.

In mid-1999, a catastrophic fire consumed the House of Peace entirely, destroying the bloodline’s founder, most of its members, and the secrets of maintaining ma’at that the Children had guarded for millennia — a disaster that coincided suspiciously with the shattering of the Rite of the Sun King the same year. One devout resident, Abu al-Intiqam (“the Light Bringer”), survived by virtue of his total devotion to his progenitor’s teachings: rather than perishing in the flame, he was restored to full mortality, retaining all his memories of centuries as one of the Damned. He now spends his remaining, drastically shortened lifespan on a singular mission to destroy the Kindred of Cairo who embrace the Beast rather than seek its annihilation, and has begun reaching out to the Sayyadin of the Dar el-Adil in preparation for a direct confrontation with the city’s undead.

vtmlarp.source: Cairo by Night, Chapters Three through Five and Appendix
